title: Vandal damages New York bank over ties to Israeli weapons firm
seoTitle: New York protest over Israeli weapons firm

tea.why: Protesters and a direct-action network opposed a bank's financial ties and loans to an Israeli defense manufacturer.
tea.want: They demanded that financial institutions cut ties and loans with Elbit Systems.
tea.changed: Oct 20: The NYPD Hate Crime Task Force continued investigating the incident after Palestine Action claimed responsibility.

summary: On Monday morning, October 19, 2026, a vandal targeted a Capital One bank branch on East 86th Street in Manhattan's Upper East Side. According to police, the suspect broke windows and spray-painted red graffiti on the glass doors referencing Palestine Action and Elbit Systems, an Israeli defense manufacturer. Palestine Action later claimed responsibility for the incident in a statement, citing the bank's loans and financial involvement with the company. The action followed previous demonstrations by groups like Demilitarize Brooklyn Navy Yard against the bank's financial backing of the defense firm. City officials condemned the incident, and the New York Police Department's Hate Crime Task Force launched an investigation.
demands: Cut financial ties with Elbit Systems
End loans to Israeli defense suppliers
response: According to police, officers responded to the scene at 7:40 a.m. No immediate arrests were made, and the NYPD Hate Crime Task Force opened an investigation. City Council Speaker Julie Menin and Councilmember Virginia Maloney condemned the incident.

updates.text: A vandal damaged windows and left graffiti at a Capital One branch on the Upper East Side, according to the NYPD.
Palestine Action claimed responsibility for the property damage in a statement sent to media.
